say: The famous run to Athens? Herodotus never mentions it. Here's the run he did record.
src: Not in Herodotus; the Athens run appears centuries later (Plutarch, Lucian).

say: Before the battle, Athens sent a runner, Pheidippides, to Sparta for help.
src: Hdt. 6.105.1: sent by the generals before leaving the city; a hemerodromos (professional day-runner).

say: About a hundred and fifty miles, over mountains. He was in Sparta the day after he left.
src: Hdt. 6.106.1 (arrived the day after leaving Athens); ~240 km / 150 mi is the modern route estimate.

say: On the way, he said, the god Pan called out to him.
His message: Eretria has fallen. Don't let Athens be next.
Sparta said yes. But not yet. Their law said no march before the full moon.
When two thousand Spartans finally arrived, the battle was over. All they could do was walk the field, and praise Athens.
src: Hdt. 6.120 (came after the full moon, reached Attica on the third day, viewed the Persian dead, praised the Athenians).
